activities.caption: rebuild the supply ladder, cheapest rung first
activities.name: wrpLadderOrder

config.prompt: The supply ladder, in the order its economics demand (roughly 1 : 3 : 10):
items: Reuse — wastewater recycled to drinking standards
config.why: Agriculture takes about 70% of global withdrawals, which is why irrigation efficiency is the biggest lever; Singapore's NEWater recycles to drinking standards and Israel draws a large share of its municipal water from the sea — but both sit above the cheaper rungs in cost.

activities.caption: bet before you read on — the running-out claim
activities.name: wrpFixedPredict

config.q: Headlines say humanity is running out of water. Is Earth running out of water?
choices: Yes — aquifers are draining and the planet is drying
No — the total is essentially fixed; what varies is where and when the usable slice arrives
Yes in rich countries, no in poor ones
config.why: Scarcity is local and temporal: about 4 billion people run short at least one month a year while their region floods in another season — a management and infrastructure problem, not a planetary shortfall.

activities.caption: file each polluter: pipe or field
activities.name: wrpSourceBuckets

config.prompt: Point source or nonpoint — file each polluter:

items.label: oil and metals washed off roads

config.why: A pipe is discrete, measurable and regulable — the Clean Water Act's permits transformed rich-world rivers; you cannot pipe a whole watershed to a treatment plant, which is why nonpoint now leads in developed countries.

activities.caption: pair each indicator with the failure it catches
activities.name: wrpIndicatorMatch

config.prompt: Five water-quality indicators, five failures — pair them:

pairs.right: the master variable for aquatic life — below about 5 mg/L fish species thin out
how much oxygen microbes will consume decomposing the organic load
catch acid inputs — mining drainage runs at pH 2–4
the cheap total-salts tripwire that flags almost any industrial leak

config.why: Pollution is a difference, and you measure the difference: DO and BOD above and below an outfall is not a school ritual but the actual logic of pollution forensics.

activities.caption: the reservoir manager's summer — trace each path
activities.name: wrpLakeBranch

config.root: You manage a drinking-water reservoir. Spring sampling shows nutrient levels climbing and last summer the water tasted of algae.

start.text: The first warm week arrives. What is your programme for the season?

choices.label: Close the nutrient tap — fertiliser timing upstream, buffer strips, sewage upgrades
choices.feedback: Attack the input, and the cascade can run backwards.

choices.label: Treat the symptoms — harvest blooms, aerate the water column
choices.feedback: Buys a clearer August, but the fertilised water returns next spring.

choices.label: Wait it out — algal blooms are natural events
choices.feedback: Cultural eutrophication is not natural ageing — it is an artificial acceleration.

tap.text: Lake Washington recovered dramatically after sewage diversion in the 1960s — the textbook demonstration that the cascade runs backwards as readily as forwards.

symptom.text: Clear water turns algal again as the nutrients keep arriving; tolerant species shift in, and cyanobacteria blooms can produce liver and nerve toxins in the drinking supply.

wait.text: Ages a lake artificially: species shift toward tolerant forms, drinking water acquires taste and toxin problems — and the fix you declined keeps getting more expensive.

config.why: The remedy is input control — the cascade from fertiliser to dead zone is the best-worked chain in water science, and it is reversible.

activities.anchor: the field's hardest case because of timescales
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the aquifer briefing
activities.name: wrpAquiferSpot

config.prompt: A briefing on groundwater contamination contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Groundwater moves metres per year, not kilometres per day.
An aquifer may take decades to centuries to flush.
Dense industrial solvents like TCE float on top of the water table, where they evaporate within months.
Nitrate plumes from fertiliser and septic systems persist long after their sources stop.
Over-pumping coastal aquifers lets the sea seep in — effectively irreversible on human timescales.
config.correction: TCE and its cousins are dense liquids that sink through the water table and sit on the aquifer floor, dissolving for decades.
config.why: Slow pollution is expensive pollution: remediation costs more than prevention by orders of magnitude, which is why source control is written into law.

activities.anchor: The historical through-line of water management is disease
activities.caption: true or false — the four water-disease routes
activities.name: wrpDiseaseJudge

statements.s: Water-washed diseases such as trachoma are solved by water quantity, not quality.
statements.why: They spread where water is too scarce for washing — the remedy is more clean water, not cleaner water.

statements.s: John Snow's 1854 Broad Street pump investigation founded both epidemiology and the practice of treating supply.
statements.why: Cholera travelled in the water people drank — the pump handle came out, and a science began.

statements.s: Schistosomiasis is caught by drinking contaminated water.
statements.why: It is a water-based parasite spending part of its life in snails in slow water — a contact hazard, not a drinking hazard.

statements.s: Chlorination of city drinking water at scale began in the 19th century.
statements.why: First at scale: Jersey City, 1908 — coagulation, sand filtration and chlorination became one of history's great life-extension technologies.

activities.caption: two oil loads, one ocean — drag between them
activities.name: wrpOilCompare

config.prompt: Which oil input dominates? Drag the divider:

before.label: chronic input — most of it
before.text: Urban runoff and shipping operational discharge, arriving every day, everywhere — diffuse, unphotographed, and collectively the larger load.

after.label: episodic spills — the news
after.text: Tanker accidents: spectacular, concentrated, and the trigger for response tech — skimming, in-situ burning, dispersants, bioremediation. Exxon Valdez's shoreline still held pockets of oil a quarter-century on.

config.why: The chronic, diffuse input dwarfs the spectacular one — the same policy shape plastic pollution shows, and the same conclusion: the durable fix is upstream design rather than downstream heroics.
